# Claudette's 2025 Outside Memory

## Welcome Message

Welcome, Claudette! Over the past year, you've been an exceptional member of the Outside community—logging over 2,200 engagements across our properties and exploring everything from snowy mountain peaks to the nuances of endurance training. Your curiosity, consistency, and genuine passion for outdoor adventure have made you a valued part of what we do.

---

## Claudette's 2025 Outside Journey

Your engagement story throughout 2025 is one of deepening commitment and evolving interests. You started the year thoughtfully in January and February, exploring foundational content like our "Intro to Skiing" course and beginning to build your reading rhythm. These early months set the tone for what would become an increasingly active engagement with our platform, particularly around cycling events and athletic training.

Spring brought a significant shift in your activity patterns. March through May saw your engagement accelerate dramatically, with May recording 246 events—a clear signal that seasonal outdoor opportunities were drawing you deeper into our content. This period coincided with your exploration of race registration platforms (BikeReg, RunReg), suggesting you were moving from passive content consumption to active participation in outdoor events. Your engagement with authors like Lisa Jhung and Frederick Dreier increased during this time, particularly around cycling and running content.

Summer became your peak engagement season. June exploded with 357 events, followed by an even more remarkable September with 498 events—your most active month of the entire year. During these months, you consumed content across multiple verticals: you dove into Everest coverage (particularly the "everest2025" tag), explored search and rescue stories, and consumed extensive training and nutrition guidance. Your Tuesday and Friday reading habits intensified during this period, suggesting you were using Outside Online as both a planning and inspiration resource for your weekend adventures.

By fall, your patterns settled into a more sustainable rhythm, though still robust. October maintained strong engagement at 165 events, while November and December naturally tapered—a realistic reflection of seasonal shifts in outdoor activity. January 2026 showed renewed momentum at 147 events, indicating you're heading into the new year with the same enthusiasm that characterized your peak months.

---

## Your Passions

• **Running & Trail Running** — With 31 events tagged "running," you're deeply invested in this discipline. You've engaged with content about training resilience, pre-race workouts, and race registration across multiple marathons and festivals, including the Clearwater Marathon and Sunflower Relay.

• **Cycling Culture & Competition** — Your 145 events on BikeReg and engagement with VeloNews (45 events) reveal a serious cyclist. You've explored gravel bike discussions, mountain biking access issues, and AI coaching technology, while actively registering for events like the Golden Nugget Criterium and Ice Weasels races.

• **Alpine & Mountaineering Adventure** — The Everest coverage dominated your 2025 reading with 15 events tagged "everest" and 11 specifically for "everest2025." Your interest extends to Grand Teton and Glacier National Parks, reflecting a passion for high-altitude and backcountry exploration.

• **Search & Rescue & Outdoor Safety** — You engaged with 25 events tagged "search and rescue," demonstrating concern for both personal safety and community welfare in outdoor spaces. Stories like "Why Do So Many People Get Into Trouble While Hiking in Hawaii?" captured your attention.

• **Endurance Training & Sports Nutrition** — Your 9 events tagged "nutrition" and consistent engagement with training content reveal a data-driven approach to athletic performance. You've read extensively about breakfast timing, Costco nutrition for athletes, and training physiological resilience.

• **Skiing & Winter Sports** — Your engagement with ski-focused content and activity posts from athletes like Heather Dietrick (featuring skate skiing adventures) shows deep appreciation for winter recreation, from backcountry exploration to groomed trails.

---

## Your Reading Habits

Your reading patterns reveal a highly intentional consumer. You're most active during evening hours (9 PM is your peak with 357 events, followed by 8 PM with 338 events), suggesting you use Outside Online as evening wind-down content—planning tomorrow's adventure or reflecting on today's. Afternoons (3–5 PM) also see significant activity with 245–117 events, likely representing lunch breaks or planning sessions during your workday.

Tuesdays dominate your weekly rhythm with a remarkable 801 events, followed by Fridays with 484 events. This pattern suggests you're using Outside Online strategically: Tuesdays for mid-week inspiration and planning, Fridays for weekend adventure preparation. Your weekend engagement drops sharply (41 events on Saturday, 39 on Sunday), indicating you're actually *outside* rather than reading about it—the mark of a true power user.

Your favorite authors—Lisa Jhung and Frederick Dreier (7 events each), followed by Jen Murphy (6 events)—have earned your trust through consistent, authoritative storytelling. You've encountered 27 unique authors and 318 unique articles across 141 different tags, demonstrating both breadth of curiosity and depth of focus. Your engagement with evergreen content (23 events) alongside breaking news (46 events) shows you value both timeless guidance and current events in the outdoor world.
